edna: The woman returning from the beach
The woman approaching the cottage beneath the sunshade with a young companion.
leonce: The man in the opening scene
The man whose morning is unfolding amid the noisy birds and holiday company.
robert: The young man accompanying Mrs. Pontellier back from the beach.
adele: The woman introduced as an example of the devoted mothers around Edna.
reisz: The woman Robert proposes asking to play for Edna.
arobin: A man Robert invokes while replying to Adèle’s warning about his behavior.
madame-lebrun: The woman at the holiday house
The woman who owns the noisy birds at the main house.
victor: The young man with the carriage
The young man Robert notices preparing to drive away.
raoul: One of the two young sons in the family staying at the cottages.
etienne: The younger of Edna’s two sons.
farival-twins: The pair of girls introduced among the company at the holiday house.
farival: The older man to whom Adèle speaks so freely.
lady-black: The woman dressed in black near the cottages.
lovers: The young couple keeping close company with each other.
nurse: The woman caring for the boys
The nurse accompanying the two Pontellier children.
father: The father Edna speaks about while recalling her earlier life.
mother: The mother Robert asks about as Edna describes her family.
janet: The sister mentioned while Edna considers a wedding present.
margaret: The older sister Edna recalls alongside her younger sister Janet.
grandmother: The grandmother with whom Edna’s children have stayed.
alphonse: The husband Robert mentions while teasing Adèle about his past attentions.
duvigne: A woman from Robert’s earlier summers
A woman Robert attended during earlier summers at Grand Isle.
beaudelet: The man associated with the guests’ boat crossing to church.
mariequita: The young Spanish-speaking girl carrying a basket on the boat to church.
antoine: The woman whose home Robert suggests
The island woman whose home Robert proposes as a place for Edna to rest.
tonie: An acquaintance Robert proposes asking to help with his boat.
monsieur-lebrun: The father Robert’s mother wishes had lived.
montel: The man Robert asks his mother for news of.
francisco: A man Mariequita mentions while discussing married people and sweethearts.
sylvano: The husband named in Mariequita’s account of an elopement.
sylvano-wife: The married woman in the elopement Mariequita describes.
fochel: The priest mentioned in connection with the lady in black’s prayer beads.
consul-wife: The married woman named in Robert’s anecdote about Arobin at Biloxi.
tenor: The opera singer Robert brings into his string of anecdotes.
joe: The servant Edna instructed to answer her afternoon callers.
belthrop-wife: One of the women Léonce asks about after Edna missed her reception afternoon.
belthrop: The husband of the woman whose visit Léonce does not want Edna to dismiss.
delasidas: The women named on one of the visiting cards Léonce reads aloud.
highcamp: One of the women named on the visiting cards left during Edna’s absence.
highcamp-husband: The husband in the household where Edna is dining after the races.
highcamp-daughter: The daughter in the household entertaining Edna after the races.
laforce: One of the women whose visiting cards Léonce reads aloud.
wiggs: One of the women whose visiting cards Léonce reads aloud.
boltons: One of the women whose visiting cards Léonce reads aloud.
cite: The woman Adèle calls upon to take over the laundry sorting.
laidpore: The artist Edna considers studying with
The person Edna mentions as a possible teacher while discussing her sketches.
pouponne: The woman at the old address
The woman Edna encounters at the house where she expected to find the pianist.
doctor: Léonce’s old friend and the Pontelliers’ family doctor.
merriman-wife: One of the women mentioned in the account of Edna’s afternoon at the racecourse.
merriman: The man attending Edna’s farewell dinner with his wife.
celestine: The woman Edna plans to employ
The older woman Edna mentions while explaining how she would manage her small house.
ellen: The maid helping with the move
The household maid working beside Edna as she prepares to leave the large house.
mayblunt: One of the guests gathered for Edna’s farewell dinner.
gouvernail: The gentleman accompanying the woman with the lorgnettes to Edna’s dinner.
laitner: The name in the law firm
One of the names in the law partnership mentioned during dinner.
jasper: The uncle mentioned in the children’s account of their country adventures.
lidie: A woman in the boys’ country surroundings
A woman named as the children describe their stay in Iberville.
susie: A woman in the boys’ country surroundings
The older woman named as the boys describe their play and errands in Iberville.
catiche: The woman at the garden eating place
The woman serving the coffee Robert remembers at Edna’s quiet retreat.
josephine: The nurse attending Adèle during labor.
celina: The woman named in Mariequita’s threat
A married woman Mariequita invokes while trying to make Victor jealous.
celina-husband: The man Mariequita threatens to run away with
The married man Mariequita names while teasing Victor about his admiration for Edna.
philomel: The cook Victor mentions while arranging Edna’s unexpected stay.
philomel-mother: The woman Victor proposes bringing in to help with the cooking.
cavalry-officer: The man in Edna’s childhood memory
The officer Edna recalls being fascinated by as a child.
engaged-man: The man in Edna’s early recollections
The young man already promised to another woman when Edna became fond of him.
tragedian: The tragic actor whose image occupied Edna’s imagination as a young woman.
school-friend: The girl remembered as Edna’s closest friend at school.
sewing-girl: The girl working the sewing machine
The young girl beside Madame Lebrun as she works at her sewing machine.
daudet: The author named as Robert recalls reading aloud for Adèle.
napoleon: The figure used to describe the appearance of the cavalry officer Edna admired.
goncourt: The name of the borrowed reading
The name Madame Lebrun uses for a book she has promised to lend Edna.
chopin: The composer named in the guests’ praise of the pianist’s performance.
isolde: The figure named in the love music the pianist plays while Edna reads.
emerson: The author Edna turns to during her evening alone in the library.
dante: The author whose work was being read at the gathering Miss Highcamp attended.
grieg: The composer of the pieces Miss Highcamp plays after dinner.
beethoven: The figure represented in the bust
The figure represented by the dusty bust in the pianist’s room.
venus: The figure Victor invokes while describing Edna’s beauty at her dinner.
virgin: The sacred figure in a comparison
The sacred figure evoked as Edna gazes at Adèle’s beauty.
holy-ghost: The sacred figure in the narrator’s aside
The sacred figure invoked in the narrator’s comment about wisdom.
pontelliers: Edna, her husband, and their two young boys.
ratignolles: Adèle and her husband, the couple holidaying alongside Edna’s family.
lebruns: The family at the holiday house
The family whose house and cottages receive the summer guests.
gluglu: The name in the boys’ country story
The name mentioned as the boys describe riding to the mill.
